comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Covenants and Credit Agreement Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: The indentures governing AMD's senior notes and the Assumed Xilinx Notes, along with its $3.0 billion Revolving Credit Agreement, impose covenants that restrict AMD's ability to incur liens, enter into sale-leaseback transactions, merge, or sell substantially all assets. The Revolving Credit Agreement also requires maintenance of a minimum interest coverage ratio and includes cross-default provisions that could accelerate debt repayment if AMD defaults on other material indebtedness, creating liquidity risk if lenders accelerate borrowings.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose risks associated with their senior notes and related credit agreements in the context of financial condition and operational flexibility. NVIDIA specifically highlights the risk of refinancing existing notes ($9.7 billion outstanding) at less favorable terms or being unable to refinance, which could adversely affect its financial condition. AMD discloses that the agreements governing its notes (including Assumed Xilinx Notes) and Revolving Credit Agreement impose covenants and restrictions (e.g., limits on liens, mergers, asset sales) that may adversely affect its ability to operate its business. While NVIDIA focuses on the market/execution risk of refinancing maturity obligations, AMD focuses on the contractual restrictions (covenants) inherent in those debt instruments, though both identify the debt agreements as a source of operational or financial risk.

sentences.text: If we decide to refinance, we may receive less favorable terms, or we may be unable to refinance at all, which may adversely affect our financial condition.

The agreements governing our notes, our guarantee of the Assumed Xilinx Notes, and our Revolving Credit Agreement impose restrictions on us that may adversely affect our ability to operate our business.
